newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel ally backs EMU delay over weak criteria.
newsitem.headline: Waigel ally backs EMU delay over weak criteria.

text.p: A leading Bavarian ally of German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said in an interview on Monday that Europe's monetary union (EMU) should be delayed rather than started with weakened criteria.

Alois Glueck, majority floor leader in the Bavarian state legislature for Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU), said the euro could be launched only if participating states fulfilled the stability criteria.
"A European currency with weakened criteria would be much more damaging for Europe than a delay in the date for the European single currency," he told the Saarbruecker Zeitung.

Waigel, who is also CSU chairman, has long insisted on a strict interpretation of the Maastricht treaty's three percent deficit-to-GDP target but now finds it difficult to stick to it himself. He says Bonn will meet the criteria on time.
Other leaders of the CSU, the conservative govering party in the rich southern state, demand strict adherence to the criteria but usually avoid the issue of a delay.
Glueck said that insisting on launching EMU as planned in 1999 or not at all was the wrong way to approach the issue.
"One puts oneself unnecessarily under pressure and in the end one has to act against one's own intentions," he said. "That can't work well."
Glueck said CSU leaders were in complete agreement about EMU.
